question: What is the atomic number of chromium?
solution:
The correct answer is __**24**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Atomic number

 
 
• It is the number of a chemical element in the periodic system, whereby the elements are arranged in order of increasing the number of protons in the nucleus.
 
• Accordingly, the number of protons, which is always equal to the number of electrons in the neutral atom, is also the atomic number.
 
• The atomic number (Z) of an element is the number of protons in the nucleus of each atom of that element. Hence, Option 2 is correct.
 
• This means that the number of protons is the characteristic that makes each element unique compared to all other elements.
 
• Elements are different because of their atomic number.
 
• The periodic table displays all of the known elements and is arranged in order of increasing atomic number.
 
• In this table, an element’s atomic number is indicated above the elemental symbol.
